classification.difficultyReason: Recognise that infinitely many integer roots violate every nonzero polynomial's finite root bound, forcing the zero polynomial.

content.prompt:
A polynomial function has every integer as a zero.

Does this mean that all real numbers are also zeroes?

answer.short: Yes. Infinitely many zeroes force the polynomial to be the zero polynomial, so every real number is a zero.
answer.worked: A nonzero polynomial of degree $n$ has at most $n$ distinct zeroes. Every integer being a zero gives infinitely many distinct zeroes, so $P(x)$ must be the zero polynomial. Hence $P(x)=0$ for every real $x$, and all real numbers are zeroes.
